key_insight: Procedural skills in LLM agents can both help and hurt, and the best skills are often the ones that cause fewer regressions rather than the ones that add the most gains.
engineering_relevance: For reliable agent design, evaluate skills by separating wins from regressions and strengthen grounding and verification, not just procedural instructions.
method: Compared agent runs with and without skills across nearly 6,000 trials.
Analyzed two office-automation benchmarks and three model harness stacks.
Decomposed outcomes into regressions and residual failures, then traced three regression modes.
evidence_signal: The study spans nearly 6,000 runs across two benchmarks and three stacks, showing regressions are substantial and can dominate apparent skill improvements.
watch_item: Skill effects can be distorted by context and trace/evaluation artifacts, so regression measurements need careful experimental control.
paper_title: The Regression Tax: Decomposing Why Skills Help and Hurt LLM Agents
